about: Access cases that run unchanged against the Python service (tests/test_access_parity.py) and the Worker (tests/workerd_access_parity.mjs). Each case starts from an empty fabric with an operator key named admin and the queues below. Example data only.

steps.session: Open a tracked anonymous session and remember it under this name.
steps.signup: Sign up a requester (optional profile overrides) and remember its key under this name.
steps.key: Have the operator issue a keyed principal with the given grant.
steps.as: Send one request as a named principal (or none) and check its status and JSON.
steps.templates: {name.field} is replaced by a remembered value; a string that is only a template keeps the value's type.

cases.title: Sign-up keeps Arabic harakat, composes decomposed accents (NFC) and keeps zero-width joiners
Sign-up still refuses control and format characters, and drops other symbols as before
The personal-data screen reads Arabic-Indic and full-width digits and full-width domains the same way in both implementations
Non-finite and inexact numbers are refused whether or not the body says it is JSON
An enqueue replay returns the first task only when it is the same request from the same principal
Both implementations publish the same requester profile rules in connect.json

requester.profile_rules.kept: letters, combining marks and digits of any script (Unicode L, M and N), the zero-width joiners U+200C and U+200D, spaces and _ . , & ' ( ) / : + -
requester.profile_rules.length_unit: Unicode code points, after normalization and removal
requester.profile_rules.refused: control and format characters (Unicode Cc and Cf) other than U+200C and U+200D, and personal or payment data
requester.profile_rules.removed: every other character, before lengths are counted

cases.title: Open verbs stay reachable behind more than 1,000 hidden ones, page by page
A JSON body nests at most 64 levels and holds only well-formed Unicode, in both implementations
A caller names at most 64 tags of at most 128 characters, on tasks, records and split children
Bad record keys, store names and numbers are the client's mistake: 400 in both implementations, never 500
HEAD answers wherever GET does, with GET's status and no body
A path with a cut-short or non-UTF-8 percent escape is the client's mistake, not a 500
Write routes answer other methods with 405 and Allow: POST, and an unknown path is not echoed at length
Lengths count code points in both implementations, and an object key with a trailing newline is refused
